summary: The first humans to walk on Mars are sitting in a classroom today, looking up at the sky. Project Ares was built to keep that dream alive: an interactive visual logbook (scrollytelling) and immersive demo taking kids and young people from liftoff to building the first robotic homes on the Red Planet, proudly highlighting Peru's scientific contributions and Andean potato research alongside NASA. Free of jargon or barriers, we turn space exploration into a relatable adventure—sparking the curiosity of the next generation of explorers who will shape the future both on Mars and here on Earth.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?Project Ares is an interactive web platform combining a cinematic visual travel logbook (scrollytelling) with an immersive demo of the first crewed mission to Mars. As users scroll, they experience five narrative chapters: launchpad boarding, cabin preparation, orbital ascent, touchdown in Jezero Crater, and building Martian habitats with autonomous robots. At the end, an interactive demo lets visitors freely explore every mission phase.

Benefits and intended impact

  • Accessible science: Translates NASA aerospace engineering into a relatable, jargon-free story for kids and young adults.
  • Reigniting STEM curiosity: Tackles declining youth interest in space careers through real-world inspiration, including Peruvian contributions like Andean potato research conducted alongside NASA.
  • Scalable reach: Runs smoothly in any browser without specialized hardware, making it easy to share in schools and homes.

Tools and technologies used Built with React, TypeScript, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion for 60 FPS animations, integrating custom SVG graphics, AI-generated cinematic videos, and AI-assisted development workflows (Google AI Studio, Gemini, and Claude).

Creativity and key considerations Instead of a static textbook, we crafted a first-person expedition journal inspired by modern space cinema, pairing frosted spatial glass cards with full-screen video transitions. Key priorities included age-appropriate storytelling, NASA Moon to Mars accuracy, and seamless mobile and desktop performance.
